questions.question: Fred Ott’s Sneeze was produced by a). Lumière brothers b). Edison’s company c). Méliès d). Porter
questions.solution_html:
• Edison's Contribution to the Commercialisation of Cinema
  • Thomas Edison and his laboratory developed the Kinetoscope (1891), a peep-hole device that allowed
  • individual viewers to watch short films, establishing the commercial potential of moving images
  • Edison's company produced some of the earliest filmed content, including Fred Ott's Sneeze (1894), and built
  • the Black Maria — the first dedicated film production studio
  • By controlling key patents through the Motion Picture Patents Company (MPPC), Edison shaped the early
  • commercial structure of the film industry, though his model was eventually displaced by the Hollywood
  • studio system
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: studio system

questions.question: Review and criticism differ because criticism a). Ignores meaning b). Avoids opinion c). Gives deeper analysis d). Only summarizes story
questions.solution_html:
• Review vs. Summary
  • A summary is a neutral, objective retelling of a film's plot — describing what happens in the story without
  • offering evaluative judgement or analytical insight
  • A review combines a brief account of the film's content with the critic's informed evaluation of its artistic
  • technical, and thematic qualities, including performance, direction, screenplay, and cinematography
  • While a summary serves only to inform about plot events, a review guides audience decision-making and
  • contributes to critical discourse about the film as a cultural and artistic work
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: contributes to critical discourse about the film as a cultural and artistic work

questions.question: Estimation is done before a). Distribution b). Shooting c). Release d). Review
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of Marketing in Film Distribution
  • Marketing creates audience awareness and anticipation for a film through trailers, posters, press tours, social
  • media campaigns, and promotional events before and during release

  • critical period — by generating sufficient public interest to drive theatre attendance
  • Marketing also positions the film for its target demographic, manages critical reception expectations, and
  • extends the film's commercial life through ancillary markets including OTT platforms, home video, and
  • merchandise

questions.question: Symbolism in film helps to a). Hide meaning b). Avoid visuals c). Reduce emotion d). Add deeper meaning
questions.solution_html:
• Importance of Film Analysis in Understanding Cinema
  • Application level – (Possible points) - Film analysis is the systematic examination of a film's formal elements
  • narrative structure, cinematography, editing, sound, performance, and mise-en-scène — to understand
  • how meaning is constructed and communicated to audiences
  • It moves the viewer beyond passive consumption to active critical engagement, revealing how filmmakers
  • use the grammar of cinema — shot selection, colour, music, framing — to guide emotional response and
  • convey ideology. Analysing narrative structure through frameworks such as three-act structure, the hero's
  • journey, or non-linear storytelling helps students understand how films create dramatic tension, character
  • development, and thematic coherence
  • Film analysis situates individual films within their historical, cultural, and political contexts — understanding
  • Pather Panchali requires knowledge of post-independence India; reading Metropolis demands awareness of
  • Weimar-era anxieties about industrialisation and class.
  • Genre analysis reveals how films both conform to and subvert audience expectations, while auteur theory
  • allows analysis of a filmmaker's recurring stylistic and thematic concerns across a body of work.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: allows analysis of a filmmaker's recurring stylistic and thematic concerns across a body of work.

questions.question: Discuss the conventions of the horror genre.
questions.solution_html:
• Horror films conventionally feature a threatening antagonist — monster, ghost, serial killer, or supernatural
  • force — that disrupts the safety and normalcy of the protagonists' world
  • Standard conventions include isolated settings, darkness, suspenseful music and sound design, jump scares
  • and the gradual revelation of danger to build dread
  • The genre typically follows a structure in which order is disrupted by evil, characters are eliminated one by
  • one, and a final confrontation determines survival — often with an ambiguous or shocking conclusion
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: one, and a final confrontation determines survival — often with an ambiguous or shocking conclusion

questions.question: Explain Persistence of vision.
questions.solution_html:
• Persistence of vision is the physiological phenomenon whereby the human eye retains an image on the retina
  • for a fraction of a second after the image has disappeared
  • When a rapid sequence of still images is projected — typically at 24 frames per second — this retention
  • creates the illusion of continuous, smooth motion
  • This optical principle is the foundational scientific basis upon which cinema and all moving image media
  • operate, allowing static photographs to create the perception of life and movement
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: operate, allowing static photographs to create the perception of life and movement

questions.question: Discuss the role of long takes in cinematic storytelling.
questions.solution_html:
• A long take is an uninterrupted shot of extended duration that allows action to unfold in real time without
  • the intervention of editing cuts
  • Long takes create a sense of realism and spatial continuity, immersing the viewer in the scene and allowing
  • performances to develop naturally without fragmentation
  • Directors such as Orson Welles, Alfonso Cuarón, and Andrei Tarkovsky used long takes as expressive tools to
  • build tension, demonstrate directorial control, and establish an observational, contemplative relationship
  • between the camera and its subjects
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: between the camera and its subjects

questions.question: Define the term 'script'.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition of Script
  • A script, or screenplay, is the written document that serves as the blueprint for a film, containing all dialogue
  • scene descriptions, character directions, and narrative structure
  • It is the primary creative document from which all departments — direction, production design, acting
  • cinematography — derive their work
  • Scripts follow a standardised format with scene headings (sluglines), action lines, and character dialogue, and
  • exist in various stages including the treatment, first draft, and shooting script
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: exist in various stages including the treatment, first draft, and shooting script

questions.question: Distinguish between practical effects and digital effects.
questions.solution_html:
• Practical effects are physical, real-world techniques achieved on set during production — including
  • miniatures, prosthetics, makeup, pyrotechnics, mechanical rigs, and in-camera optical illusions
  • Digital effects (VFX) are created in post-production using computer-generated imagery (CGI) to add, enhance
  • or replace visual elements that were not present during filming
  • Practical effects offer tangible realism and interact authentically with actors and lighting, while digital effects
  • provide limitless creative possibilities; contemporary filmmaking typically combines both for optimal results
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: provide limitless creative possibilities; contemporary filmmaking typically combines both for optimal results

questions.question: Write a note on Black Maria
questions.solution_html:
• The Black Maria was the world's first purpose-built film production studio, constructed by Thomas Edison
  • and William Dickson in 1893 at Edison's laboratory complex in West Orange, New Jersey
  • The structure was covered in black tar paper — giving it its nickname — and was built on a rotating pivot that
  • allowed it to follow the sun's direction to maximise natural light on the subject being filmed
  • It was used to produce early Kinetoscope films featuring vaudeville performers, boxers, and novelty acts
  • making it the originating site of commercial film production in America
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: making it the originating site of commercial film production in America

questions.question: Explain the importance of documentation during film production.
questions.solution_html:
• Production documentation — including call sheets, shot lists, continuity reports, script supervisor notes, and
  • production reports — ensures that all departments are coordinated and working from the same information
  • Continuity documentation specifically records costume, makeup, prop placement, and actor position
  • between takes, preventing visible inconsistencies in the edited film
  • Thorough documentation protects the production legally, facilitates post-production by providing editors and
  • VFX teams with accurate records, and serves as an institutional memory for the entire filmmaking process
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: VFX teams with accurate records, and serves as an institutional memory for the entire filmmaking process

questions.question: Discuss the use of sound design in a motion picture.
questions.solution_html:
• Sound design encompasses all non-dialogue audio elements — ambient sound, sound effects, Foley, and
  • music — that together create the acoustic world of a film and guide emotional response
  • Effective sound design establishes place and atmosphere, signals danger or comfort, reinforces visual action
  • and directs audience attention to narratively significant elements within the frame
  • Sound designers use contrast, silence, and layered audio to manipulate tension and pacing; landmark sound
  • design works such as those in Apocalypse Now and Interstellar demonstrate how sound is as narratively
  • powerful as the image itself
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: powerful as the image itself

questions.question: Explain the importance of makeup continuity.
questions.solution_html:
• Makeup continuity ensures that an actor's appearance — skin tone, wounds, ageing effects, hairstyle
  • remains consistent across all shots within a scene, regardless of the order in which they are filmed
  • Since films are almost never shot in chronological sequence, continuity errors in makeup can create jarring
  • inconsistencies visible to audiences in the edited film
  • The makeup continuity supervisor maintains detailed photographic records of each actor's look for every
  • scene, enabling precise replication across shooting days and ensuring seamless narrative coherence in the
  • final cut
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: final cut

questions.question: Discuss the representation of women in contemporary Malayalam films.
questions.solution_html:
• Application level – (Possible points) - Contemporary Malayalam films increasingly feature women in
  • professional roles — journalists, police officers, doctors — and narratives that centre female desire, ambition
  • and trauma without reducing characters to male-defined functions
  • However, contradictions persist: item numbers, male gaze cinematography, and token female characters in
  • mainstream commercial films remain common, suggesting that progressive representation coexists with
  • persistent patriarchal conventions.
  • The new wave of Malayalam women filmmakers — including Anjali Menon and Geetu Mohandas — is
  • reshaping representational norms from behind the camera, ensuring that female experience is depicted with
  • authenticity and complexity

questions.question: Explain the complete process of the production stage.
questions.solution_html:
• Pre-production completion — the production stage formally begins once all pre-production elements are in
  • place: a locked script, signed cast and crew, secured locations, completed storyboards, and a detailed
  • shooting schedule prepared by the assistant director
  • Principal photography — the core of the production stage involves daily shooting according to the call sheet
  • which schedules which scenes will be filmed, which cast members are required, and what equipment is
  • needed each day
  • Direction and performance — the director works with actors to realise performances, guides the director of
  • photography on shot composition and camera movement, and makes real-time creative decisions to capture
  • the script's vision
  • Cinematography and lighting — the DoP and gaffer design and execute lighting setups for each scene
  • ensuring visual consistency, appropriate mood, and technically sound exposure throughout the shoot
  • Sound recording — the production sound mixer and boom operator capture clean dialogue and on-set audio
  • using boom microphones and lavalier mics, as poor production sound is difficult and expensive to fix in post
  • Continuity and documentation — the script supervisor monitors continuity of costume, makeup, props, and
  • performance between takes; daily production reports track footage shot, setups completed, and any
  • schedule deviations
  • Daily review — dailies (rushes) are reviewed by the director and producer at the end of each shooting day to
  • assess performance and technical quality, enabling reshoots to be scheduled before the production moves
  • on
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: on
